newsitem.title: USA: Citadel grad indicted in shooting fellow cadet.
newsitem.headline: Citadel grad indicted in shooting fellow cadet.

text.p: A Charleston County grand jury on Wednesday returned a two-count indictment against a graduate of The Citadel who confessed to shooting a fellow cadet in 1992 while they attended the military college.
George Cormeny, who graduated in 1994, was indicted for unlawful possession of a firearm by a person under 21 and for carrying a firearm in a public building.
"Our client feels nothing but remorse and regret for the tragedy which occurred on March 12, 1992," Cormeny's lawyer John Kerr said after the grand jury hearing.
"The shooting of his fellow cadet was a terrible, unintentional accident but George realises there are consequences, even to unintentional accidents," Kerr added.
Cormeny was not formally served with the indictments on Wednesday and the case had not been turned over to local authorities as the solicitor was out of town.
He never told anyone about the March 12, 1992, shooting that badly wounded then-cadet Berra Byrd in the chest.
Both men graduated in 1994, and Cormeny enrolled in a seminary in Pennsylvania to become an Episcopal priest while Byrd became a banker in Greenville, South Carolina.
But the NAACP, acting on behalf of Byrd, had called for a federal investigation.
Byrd is black and Cormeny is white.

The investigation led to Cormeny who withdrew from seminary last summer, returned to Charleston and confessed in an open letter to the local newspaper, The Post and Courier, that he accidentally shot Byrd in the chest.
He said he sneaked a 9mm handgun into the barracks and inadvertently discharged it out his fourth-floor room window.
Byrd was shot at about 5:30 p.m. while walking to his roommate's car in a parking lot.
"The situation went from fright to sheer terror when I heard a scream in the distance. Running to the window, I saw a fellow cadet running across a parking lot screaming," Cormeny's confession said.
According to local newspaper reports Byrd did not see anyone and did not hear a shot, but suddenly felt pain. With a lung collapsed, he stumbled toward a building and got help.

As part of the effort to solve the mystery, the FBI contacted 1,500 people on campus at that time, including all cadets. Authorities would not reveal details of the investigation or say how Cormeny was identifed as the shooter.
Cormeny said he has personally apologised to Byrd.
